question_type: count of maturity months above a threshold across two as-of-dated Treasury Survey of Ownership bill schedules (survey as-of date vs bulletin issue month)
decisive_step: Map 'recorded on the end of month January 1977 / January 1978' to the survey AS-OF date, not the January bulletin issues: the Jan-31 surveys are printed in the March issues (treasury_bulletin_1977_03.txt TSO-3 at line 4795, bill rows 4798-4809; treasury_bulletin_1978_03.txt TSO-3 at line 4766, bill rows 4769-4780), and their 'Treasury Bills: Regular weekly and annual maturing' rows tile the requested Feb-1977..Jan-1979 window exactly, one maturity-month row per month, column 'Total amount outstanding'. The reference made this call at worklog.md Step 0 (lines 8-20) and confirmed the printing at Step 4 (worklog.md:43-46, grep of the dated section header across all issues). In v8 both wrong GLM arms took the January issues (whose TSO-3 is the Nov-30 survey) and failed here.

notes: v8 -> v9 contrast is the main lesson: v8 none/prompt failed at SOURCE_ISSUE_VINTAGE by reading the January issues (Nov-30 surveys) and then looped ~120 steps; in v9 all four cells resolved the as-of date in 2-4 find_tables calls because the listing itself says 'as-of JANUARY 31, 1977' next to 1977_03. Keep that annotation in any v10 tool rewrite. Two cells (a, b) carry failure_kind=transport_retry with 328 s and 385 s wall time for ~11-13 requests, against 25 s for b2; that is provider latency, not behaviour. Zero-byte tool output with exit 0 occurred at b2[13] (and c[14] on ordinal 13); both commands reproduce correctly offline with OFFICEQA_CORPUS/TABLES_INDEX set, so the loss is in the harness command capture - worth a guard. --grep matches label/period/section, so --grep Bills returns the whole 'Treasury Bills' segment (13 rows incl. the total, flagged PERIOD?), which here was exactly the wanted slice; document that semantics in README so models do not read '0 rows' or 'all rows' as a grep failure. Bare filenames work in show_table but a[16]'s sed on a bare filename printed nothing; the README's absolute corpus path is needed for sed/rg.
